audit_status.source_base: Hebrew Numbers / Bemidbar Passover and cloud-guidance text tradition, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for wilderness Passover, delayed observance for corpse-unclean or distant traveler, sojourner inclusion, cloud/fire presence, and movement/rest by YHWH's command.

verses.restored: YHWH spoke to Moses in wilderness of Sinai, in first month of second year after they came out from land of Egypt, saying,

familiar.text: And the LORD spake unto Moses in the wilderness of Sinai, in the first month of the second year after they were come out of the land of Egypt, saying,

modern.text: In the first month of the second year after Israel had come out of the land of Egypt, the LORD spoke to Moses in the Wilderness of Sinai:

original.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר יְהוָ֣ה אֶל מֹשֶׁ֣ה בְמִדְבַּר סִ֠ינַי בַּשָּׁנָ֨ה הַשֵּׁנִ֜ית לְצֵאתָ֨ם מֵאֶ֧רֶץ מִצְרַ֛יִם בַּחֹ֥דֶשׁ הָרִאשׁ֖וֹן לֵאמֹֽר

verses.restored: Children of Israel shall make Passover at its appointed time.

familiar.text: Let the children of Israel also keep the passover at his appointed season.

modern.text: “The Israelites are to observe the Passover at its appointed time.

original.text: וְיַעֲשׂ֧וּ בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל אֶת הַפָּ֖סַח בְּמוֹעֲדֽוֹ

verses.restored: On fourteenth day of this month, between evenings, you shall make it at its appointed time; according to all its statutes and all its judgments you shall make it.

familiar.text: In the fourteenth day of this month, at even, ye shall keep it in his appointed season: according to all the rites of it, and according to all the ceremonies thereof, shall ye keep it.

modern.text: You are to observe it at the appointed time, at twilight on the fourteenth day of this month, in accordance with its statutes and ordinances.”

original.text: בְּאַרְבָּעָ֣ה עָשָֽׂר י֠וֹם בַּחֹ֨דֶשׁ הַזֶּ֜ה בֵּ֧ין הָֽעֲרְבַּ֛יִם תַּעֲשׂ֥וּ אֹת֖וֹ בְּמוֹעֲד֑וֹ כְּכָל חֻקֹּתָ֥יו וּכְכָל מִשְׁפָּטָ֖יו תַּעֲשׂ֥וּ אֹתֽוֹ

verses.restored: Moses spoke to children of Israel to make Passover.

familiar.text: And Moses spake unto the children of Israel, that they should keep the passover.

modern.text: So Moses told the Israelites to observe the Passover,

original.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר מֹשֶׁ֛ה אֶל בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לַעֲשֹׂ֥ת הַפָּֽסַח

verses.restored: They made Passover in first month, on fourteenth day of month between evenings, in wilderness of Sinai; according to all YHWH commanded Moses, so children of Israel did.

familiar.text: And they kept the passover on the fourteenth day of the first month at even in the wilderness of Sinai: according to all that the LORD commanded Moses, so did the children of Israel.

modern.text: and they did so in the Wilderness of Sinai, at twilight on the fourteenth day of the first month. The Israelites did everything just as the LORD had commanded Moses.

original.text: וַיַּעֲשׂ֣וּ אֶת הַפֶּ֡סַח בָּרִאשׁ֡וֹן בְּאַרְבָּעָה֩ עָשָׂ֨ר י֥וֹם לַחֹ֛דֶשׁ בֵּ֥ין הָעַרְבַּ֖יִם בְּמִדְבַּ֣ר סִינָ֑י כְּ֠כֹל אֲשֶׁ֨ר צִוָּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ אֶת מֹשֶׁ֔ה כֵּ֥ן עָשׂ֖וּ בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל

verses.restored: There were men who were unclean by dead soul/life of a human and could not make Passover on that day; they came near before Moses and Aaron on that day.

familiar.text: And there were certain men, who were defiled by the dead body of a man, that they could not keep the passover on that day: and they came before Moses and before Aaron on that day:

modern.text: But there were some men who were unclean due to a dead body, so they could not observe the Passover on that day. And they came before Moses and Aaron that same day

original.text: וַיְהִ֣י אֲנָשִׁ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר הָי֤וּ טְמֵאִים֙ לְנֶ֣פֶשׁ אָדָ֔ם וְלֹא יָכְל֥וּ לַעֲשֹׂת הַפֶּ֖סַח בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא וַֽיִּקְרְב֞וּ לִפְנֵ֥י מֹשֶׁ֛ה וְלִפְנֵ֥י אַהֲרֹ֖ן בַּיּ֥וֹם הַהֽוּא

verses.restored: Those men said to him, We are unclean by dead soul/life of a human. Why should we be diminished, not bringing offering of YHWH at its appointed time among children of Israel?

familiar.text: And those men said unto him, We are defiled by the dead body of a man: wherefore are we kept back, that we may not offer an offering of the LORD in his appointed season among the children of Israel?

modern.text: and said to Moses, “We are unclean because of a dead body, but why should we be excluded from presenting the LORD’s offering with the other Israelites at the appointed time?”

original.text: וַ֠יֹּאמְרוּ הָאֲנָשִׁ֤ים הָהֵ֨מָּה֙ אֵלָ֔יו אֲנַ֥חְנוּ טְמֵאִ֖ים לְנֶ֣פֶשׁ אָדָ֑ם לָ֣מָּה נִגָּרַ֗ע לְבִלְתִּ֨י הַקְרִ֜ב אֶת קָרְבַּ֤ן יְהוָה֙ בְּמֹ֣עֲד֔וֹ בְּת֖וֹךְ בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל

verses.restored: Moses said to them, Stand and let me hear what YHWH commands concerning you.

familiar.text: And Moses said unto them, Stand still, and I will hear what the LORD will command concerning you.

modern.text: “Wait here until I find out what the LORD commands concerning you,” Moses replied.

original.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֖ם מֹשֶׁ֑ה עִמְד֣וּ וְאֶשְׁמְעָ֔ה מַה יְצַוֶּ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה לָכֶֽם

verses.restored: YHWH spoke to Moses, saying,

familiar.text: And the LORD spake unto Moses, saying,

modern.text: Then the LORD said to Moses,

original.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹֽר

verses.restored: Speak to children of Israel, saying: Any man among you or your generations who is unclean by dead soul/life or is on a distant journey, he shall still make Passover to YHWH.

familiar.text: Speak unto the children of Israel, saying, If any man of you or of your posterity shall be unclean by reason of a dead body, or be in a journey afar off, yet he shall keep the passover unto the LORD.

modern.text: “Tell the Israelites: ‘When any one of you or your descendants is unclean because of a dead body, or is away on a journey, he may still observe the Passover to the LORD.

original.text: דַּבֵּ֛ר אֶל בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֵאמֹ֑ר אִ֣ישׁ אִ֣ישׁ כִּי יִהְיֶֽה טָמֵ֣א לָנֶ֡פֶשׁ אוֹ֩ בְדֶ֨רֶךְ רְחֹקָ֜הׄ לָכֶ֗ם א֚וֹ לְדֹרֹ֣תֵיכֶ֔ם וְעָ֥שָׂה פֶ֖סַח לַיהוָֽה

verses.restored: In second month, on fourteenth day between evenings, they shall make it; with unleavened bread and bitter herbs they shall eat it.

familiar.text: The fourteenth day of the second month at even they shall keep it, and eat it with unleavened bread and bitter herbs.

modern.text: Such people are to observe it at twilight on the fourteenth day of the second month. They are to eat the lamb, together with unleavened bread and bitter herbs;

original.text: בַּחֹ֨דֶשׁ הַשֵּׁנִ֜י בְּאַרְבָּעָ֨ה עָשָׂ֥ר י֛וֹם בֵּ֥ין הָעַרְבַּ֖יִם יַעֲשׂ֣וּ אֹת֑וֹ עַל מַצּ֥וֹת וּמְרֹרִ֖ים יֹאכְלֻֽהוּ

verses.restored: They shall leave none of it until morning and shall not break a bone in it; according to every statute of Passover they shall make it.

familiar.text: They shall leave none of it unto the morning, nor break any bone of it: according to all the ordinances of the passover they shall keep it.

modern.text: they may not leave any of it until morning or break any of its bones. They must observe the Passover according to all its statutes.

original.text: לֹֽא יַשְׁאִ֤ירוּ מִמֶּ֨נּוּ֙ עַד בֹּ֔קֶר וְעֶ֖צֶם לֹ֣א יִשְׁבְּרוּ ב֑וֹ כְּכָל חֻקַּ֥ת הַפֶּ֖סַח יַעֲשׂ֥וּ אֹתֽוֹ

verses.restored: But the man who is clean and is not on a journey and refrains from making Passover, that soul/life shall be cut off from its people, because offering of YHWH he did not bring at its appointed time; that man shall bear his sin/misalignment.

familiar.text: But the man that is clean, and is not in a journey, and forbeareth to keep the passover, even the same soul shall be cut off from among his people: because he brought not the offering of the LORD in his appointed season, that man shall bear his sin.

modern.text: But if a man who is ceremonially clean and is not on a journey still fails to observe the Passover, he must be cut off from his people, because he did not present the LORD’s offering at its appointed time. That man will bear the consequences of his sin.

original.text: וְהָאִישׁ֩ אֲשֶׁר ה֨וּא טָה֜וֹר וּבְדֶ֣רֶךְ לֹא הָיָ֗ה וְחָדַל֙ לַעֲשׂ֣וֹת הַפֶּ֔סַח וְנִכְרְתָ֛ה הַנֶּ֥פֶשׁ הַהִ֖וא מֵֽעַמֶּ֑יהָ כִּ֣י קָרְבַּ֣ן יְהוָ֗ה לֹ֤א הִקְרִיב֙ בְּמֹ֣עֲד֔וֹ חֶטְא֥וֹ יִשָּׂ֖א הָאִ֥ישׁ הַהֽוּא

verses.restored: When a sojourner sojourns with you and makes Passover to YHWH, according to statute of Passover and according to its judgment so he shall do; one statute shall be for you, for sojourner and native of land.

familiar.text: And if a stranger shall sojourn among you, and will keep the passover unto the LORD; according to the ordinance of the passover, and according to the manner thereof, so shall he do: ye shall have one ordinance, both for the stranger, and for him that was born in the land.

modern.text: If a foreigner dwelling among you wants to observe the Passover to the LORD, he is to do so according to the Passover statute and its ordinances. You are to apply the same statute to both the foreigner and the native of the land.’” The Cloud above the Tabernacle (Exodus 40:34–38)

original.text: וְכִֽי יָג֨וּר אִתְּכֶ֜ם גֵּ֗ר וְעָ֤שָֽׂה פֶ֨סַח֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה כְּחֻקַּ֥ת הַפֶּ֛סַח וּכְמִשְׁפָּט֖וֹ כֵּ֣ן יַעֲשֶׂ֑ה חֻקָּ֤ה אַחַת֙ יִהְיֶ֣ה לָכֶ֔ם וְלַגֵּ֖ר וּלְאֶזְרַ֥ח הָאָֽרֶץ

verses.restored: On day dwelling-place was raised, cloud covered dwelling-place, tent of testimony; in evening it was over dwelling-place like appearance of fire until morning.

familiar.text: And on the day that the tabernacle was reared up the cloud covered the tabernacle, namely, the tent of the testimony: and at even there was upon the tabernacle as it were the appearance of fire, until the morning.

modern.text: On the day that the tabernacle, the Tent of the Testimony, was set up, the cloud covered it and appeared like fire above the tabernacle from evening until morning.

original.text: וּבְיוֹם֙ הָקִ֣ים אֶת הַמִּשְׁכָּ֔ן כִּסָּ֤ה הֶֽעָנָן֙ אֶת הַמִּשְׁכָּ֔ן לְאֹ֖הֶל הָעֵדֻ֑ת וּבָעֶ֜רֶב יִהְיֶ֧ה עַֽל הַמִּשְׁכָּ֛ן כְּמַרְאֵה אֵ֖שׁ עַד בֹּֽקֶר

verses.restored: So it was continually: cloud covered it, and appearance of fire by night.

familiar.text: So it was alway: the cloud covered it by day, and the appearance of fire by night.

modern.text: It remained that way continually; the cloud would cover the tabernacle by day, and at night it would appear like fire.

original.text: כֵּ֚ן יִהְיֶ֣ה תָמִ֔יד הֶעָנָ֖ן יְכַסֶּ֑נּוּ וּמַרְאֵה אֵ֖שׁ לָֽיְלָה

verses.restored: Whenever cloud was lifted from over tent, afterward children of Israel set out; and in place where cloud settled, there children of Israel camped.

familiar.text: And when the cloud was taken up from the tabernacle, then after that the children of Israel journeyed: and in the place where the cloud abode, there the children of Israel pitched their tents.

modern.text: Whenever the cloud was lifted from above the Tent, the Israelites would set out, and wherever the cloud settled, there the Israelites would camp.

original.text: וּלְפִ֞י הֵעָלֹ֤ת הֶֽעָנָן֙ מֵעַ֣ל הָאֹ֔הֶל וְאַ֣חֲרֵי כֵ֔ן יִסְע֖וּ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וּבִמְק֗וֹם אֲשֶׁ֤ר יִשְׁכָּן שָׁם֙ הֶֽעָנָ֔ן שָׁ֥ם יַחֲנ֖וּ בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל

verses.restored: At mouth/command of YHWH children of Israel set out, and at mouth/command of YHWH they camped; all days cloud settled over dwelling-place they camped.

familiar.text: At the commandment of the LORD the children of Israel journeyed, and at the commandment of the LORD they pitched: as long as the cloud abode upon the tabernacle they rested in their tents.

modern.text: At the LORD’s command the Israelites set out, and at the LORD’s command they camped. As long as the cloud remained over the tabernacle, they remained encamped.

original.text: עַל פִּ֣י יְהוָ֗ה יִסְעוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְעַל פִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה יַחֲנ֑וּ כָּל יְמֵ֗י אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִשְׁכֹּ֧ן הֶעָנָ֛ן עַל הַמִּשְׁכָּ֖ן יַחֲנֽוּ

verses.restored: When cloud prolonged over dwelling-place many days, children of Israel kept charge of YHWH and did not set out.

familiar.text: And when the cloud tarried long upon the tabernacle many days, then the children of Israel kept the charge of the LORD, and journeyed not.

modern.text: Even when the cloud lingered over the tabernacle for many days, the Israelites kept the LORD’s charge and did not set out.

original.text: וּבְהַאֲרִ֧יךְ הֶֽעָנָ֛ן עַל הַמִּשְׁכָּ֖ן יָמִ֣ים רַבִּ֑ים וְשָׁמְר֧וּ בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל אֶת מִשְׁמֶ֥רֶת יְהוָ֖ה וְלֹ֥א יִסָּֽעוּ

verses.restored: Sometimes cloud was few days over dwelling-place; at mouth/command of YHWH they camped, and at mouth/command of YHWH they set out.

familiar.text: And so it was, when the cloud was a few days upon the tabernacle; according to the commandment of the LORD they abode in their tents, and according to the commandment of the LORD they journeyed.

modern.text: Sometimes the cloud remained over the tabernacle for only a few days, and they would camp at the LORD’s command and set out at the LORD’s command.

original.text: וְיֵ֞שׁ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִהְיֶ֧ה הֶֽעָנָ֛ן יָמִ֥ים מִסְפָּ֖ר עַל הַמִּשְׁכָּ֑ן עַל פִּ֤י יְהוָה֙ יַחֲנ֔וּ וְעַל פִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה יִסָּֽעוּ

verses.restored: Sometimes cloud was from evening until morning, and cloud lifted in morning and they set out; or by day and by night, when cloud lifted they set out.

familiar.text: And so it was, when the cloud abode from even unto the morning, and that the cloud was taken up in the morning, then they journeyed: whether it was by day or by night that the cloud was taken up, they journeyed.

modern.text: Sometimes the cloud remained only from evening until morning, and when it lifted in the morning, they would set out. Whether it was by day or by night, when the cloud was taken up, they would set out.

original.text: וְיֵ֞שׁ אֲשֶׁר יִהְיֶ֤ה הֶֽעָנָן֙ מֵעֶ֣רֶב עַד בֹּ֔קֶר וְנַעֲלָ֧ה הֶֽעָנָ֛ן בַּבֹּ֖קֶר וְנָסָ֑עוּ א֚וֹ יוֹמָ֣ם וָלַ֔יְלָה וְנַעֲלָ֥ה הֶעָנָ֖ן וְנָסָֽעוּ

verses.restored: Whether two days or a month or many days, when cloud prolonged over dwelling-place, settling upon it, children of Israel camped and did not set out; when it lifted they set out.

familiar.text: Or whether it were two days, or a month, or a year, that the cloud tarried upon the tabernacle, remaining thereon, the children of Israel abode in their tents, and journeyed not: but when it was taken up, they journeyed.

modern.text: Whether the cloud lingered for two days, a month, or longer, the Israelites camped and did not set out as long as the cloud remained over the tabernacle; but when it was lifted, they would set out.

original.text: אֽוֹ יֹמַ֜יִם אוֹ חֹ֣דֶשׁ אוֹ יָמִ֗ים בְּהַאֲרִ֨יךְ הֶעָנָ֤ן עַל הַמִּשְׁכָּן֙ לִשְׁכֹּ֣ן עָלָ֔יו יַחֲנ֥וּ בְנֵֽי יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וְלֹ֣א יִסָּ֑עוּ וּבְהֵעָלֹת֖וֹ יִסָּֽעוּ

verses.restored: At mouth/command of YHWH they camped and at mouth/command of YHWH they set out; they kept charge of YHWH, at mouth/command of YHWH by hand of Moses.

familiar.text: At the commandment of the LORD they rested in the tents, and at the commandment of the LORD they journeyed: they kept the charge of the LORD, at the commandment of the LORD by the hand of Moses.

modern.text: They camped at the LORD’s command, and they set out at the LORD’s command; they carried out the LORD’s charge according to His command through Moses.

original.text: עַל פִּ֤י יְהוָה֙ יַחֲנ֔וּ וְעַל פִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה יִסָּ֑עוּ אֶת מִשְׁמֶ֤רֶת יְהוָה֙ שָׁמָ֔רוּ עַל פִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה בְּיַד מֹשֶֽׁה

translation_notes: The delayed Passover creates an accommodation rather than permanent exclusion for people made ritually unclean by caring for the dead or prevented by travel.
The affected men speak up, Moses pauses, and new instruction is sought—an important model of responsive law.
Sojourner and native share one Passover statute; this must not become xenophobic gatekeeping.
Cloud and fire guide both movement and waiting. Divine guidance includes staying put, not constant productivity.
'At the mouth of YHWH' is preserved as command/guidance language.
safety_note: Do not use Numbers 9 to shame mourners, travelers, disabled people, or those unable to meet a sacred date. The chapter itself creates a second opportunity and treats responsive accommodation as covenant faithfulness.
